top_choice_rationale: P001 (B001, Helpman and Melitz) rewards one identifiable discovery: firm heterogeneity and selection into exporting and foreign investment, with reallocation across firms as a channel for the gains from trade. Melitz (2003) and Helpman-Melitz-Yeaple (2004) are the origin of the selection model and the exports-versus-FDI sorting result. More than twenty years of firm-level data have tested the predictions, and where the baseline failed in detail the literature extended it and kept the selection logic. The main risk is attribution. Bernard, Eaton, Jensen and Kortum, and Redding's quantitative work, are outside the credited names. I judge that manageable if the citation is confined to selection and reallocation, makes no claim about welfare magnitudes, and the scientific background acknowledges the empirical precursors. The proposal is a single two-name part, which avoids fragmenting any other credit. That all eleven round-2 files back P001 is not evidence of merit, because they may share reasoning patterns. My ranking rests on the discovery boundary, maturity and attribution. A narrow Berry-Levinsohn-Pakes B006 prize would be a credible fallback, but it is not on the slate. P000 is ranked second because P001 is mature and defensibly attributed, so no award would be worse.
recusal_note: None apparent from profile for Helpman or Melitz. Per the profile, I co-authored with committee colleagues Krusell, Boppart and Friberg and am an IIES colleague of Krusell and Boppart. None of them is a credited name in P001. This is disclosed, not adjudicated.
